why.title: Why the technique works
why.p1: A fixed block gives a task a clear start and a clear end, which makes starting less daunting and drifting harder. The scheduled break keeps you from working until you are too tired to think.
why.p2: Counting finished sessions also gives you data: after a week you can see how many Pomodoros a task really takes and estimate better. It is a method, not a guarantee, so adjust the lengths to fit your work.
why.source: Source: Francesco Cirillo, The Pomodoro Technique (Currency, 2018).

q1.q: Is Study Bro free, and do I need an account?
q1.a: It is free and you do not need an account. You can start the timer straight away as a guest. Signing in is optional and lets you keep your tasks and history across devices; anything you did as a guest moves to your account when you sign in.

q2.a: A time-management method by Francesco Cirillo. You work in a fixed block (traditionally 25 minutes), take a 5-minute break, and after four blocks take a longer break of 15 to 30 minutes. The Pomodoro guide explains how to apply it.

q3.q: Can I change the timer lengths?
q3.a: Yes. In Timer settings you can set focus from 1 to 120 minutes, short break from 1 to 30, long break from 1 to 60, and how many sessions come before a long break (2 to 10). Presets cover 25/5, 50/10, 52/17 and 90/20. You can also turn auto-start for breaks and focus sessions on or off.

q4.q: How do tasks work with the timer?
q4.a: Add a task with a priority, tags and an estimate in Pomodoros, then link it to the session you are running. Finished sessions are recorded against the task, so you can compare estimates with what really happened.

q5.q: Which sounds and backgrounds are available?
q5.a: Ambient sounds such as nature, lo-fi and white noise, plus your own YouTube link. For the background you can choose a scene or your own image, and pick a digital, analog, flip or progress clock.

q6.q: How does sign-in work, and what happens to my data?
q6.a: You can sign in with a one-time code sent to your email, or with Google. In Settings, under Account, you can export your data as a JSON file or delete your account together with its tasks, sessions and tags. See the Privacy Policy for details.

q7.a: English, Vietnamese and Japanese. Change the language with the switcher in the footer.

guide2.title: The Pomodoro Technique: a practical guide
guide2.lead: What it is, how to run a session, which lengths to choose, and how to use Study Bro to do it.

what.title: What the Pomodoro Technique is
what.p1: The Pomodoro Technique is a time-management method developed by Francesco Cirillo in the late 1980s. You work in short, fixed blocks, traditionally 25 minutes, separated by short breaks. Each block is a **pomodoro**, Italian for tomato, after the tomato-shaped kitchen timer Cirillo used as a student.
what.p2: The point is not the number 25. A fixed block gives you one clear start, one clear end and one thing to work on. That makes it easier to begin and harder to drift. After four blocks you take a longer break.
what.p3: Study Bro is a Pomodoro timer built around that loop: focus, short break and long break modes, tasks you can link to sessions, and a history of what you finished.

session.title: How to run a focus session
session.intro: One round takes about half an hour. Follow these steps:

steps.1: **Pick one task.** Choose the next concrete step, such as "outline section 2", not a vague project like "thesis".
steps.2: **Link it to the session.** Select the task in Tasks (T) so the session is recorded against it.
steps.3: **Start the focus timer.** Press Space. The default is 25 minutes.
steps.4: **Work on that task only.** If something else comes to mind, write it down and go back to work.
steps.5: **Take the short break.** Five minutes away from the screen. Do not start something new.
steps.6: **Repeat, and rest longer after four.** After four focus sessions take a long break (15 minutes by default, up to 30 is common), then start a new cycle.

session.note: By default a break starts on its own when a focus session ends, but the next focus session waits until you press start. You can change both in Timer settings (C).

rhythm.title: Choosing 25/5, 50/10, 52/17 or a longer block
rhythm.intro: No single rhythm suits everyone. These are the common ones:

classic.name: Classic
classic.for: Getting started, tasks you keep avoiding, short study sessions.

extended.name: Extended
extended.for: Work that needs a warm-up: writing, coding, problem sets.

ratio.for: A ratio popularised in 2014 from a time-tracking company's analysis of its own users. Treat it as an option, not a rule.

deep.name: Deep-work block
deep.for: Demanding work you want to protect from interruption. The 90-minute figure borrows from ultradian-rhythm ideas, where the evidence is mixed.

rhythm.how: How to choose: use 25/5 for a week. If the timer rings just as you get going, move to 50/10. If you cannot make yourself start, shorten the block. Whatever you pick, keep the breaks.
rhythm.limits: In Timer settings (C) focus can be 1 to 120 minutes, a short break 1 to 30, a long break 1 to 60, and a long break can come every 2 to 10 sessions. For a 90-minute block, choose the 90/20 preset: 90 minutes of focus, then a 20-minute break.

interruptions.title: Handling interruptions
interruptions.intro: Cirillo separates two kinds of interruption, and each needs a different response.

list.1: **Internal** (you remember an email, want to check your phone): write it on paper or add it as a task, then return. It costs less to do it later than to switch now.
list.2: **External** (a colleague, a message): Cirillo's advice is to inform the person you are busy, negotiate a time, schedule it, and call back.
list.3: **Long interruptions:** in Cirillo's rules a pomodoro is indivisible. If you have to stop for real, reset the timer (R) and start a fresh block instead of pretending the broken one counts.

interruptions.outro: Silencing notifications for the length of a block removes most of both kinds.

tasks.title: Using tasks and estimates
tasks.intro: Estimate in Pomodoros rather than hours. Before you start, guess how many blocks a task needs; afterwards, compare. Your guesses improve quickly.

list.1: Split a task that looks bigger than about five to seven Pomodoros (Cirillo's guideline). Group tiny tasks into a single block.
list.2: Give each task an estimate in Pomodoros, a priority and, if you like, tags such as the course or project.
list.3: Link the task you are working on to the running session so your history shows what each session was for.
list.4: Move a task to In progress when you start and Done when it is finished, and filter the list by status or date.

breaks.title: Taking breaks that work
breaks.intro: A break only helps if it lets your attention recover.

list.1: Stand up and move, even for a minute.
list.2: Drink water and look at something far away to rest your eyes.
list.3: Avoid feeds, chats and anything that starts another thread of thought.
list.4: If you want something playful, the arcade has short games (G). Stop when the break ends.

breaks.outro: The long break after four sessions is for a proper change of scene: a walk, a snack, a stretch.

list.1: **Sounds (S):** nature sounds, lo-fi and white noise, or your own YouTube link. Try them at low volume; silence works too.
list.2: **Scenes (B):** change the background and the clock style (digital, analog, flip or progress).
list.3: **Stats (H):** focus time by day, week and month, and your daily streak. Use it to see your real rhythm, not to chase numbers.
list.4: **No account needed:** everything works as a guest. Sign in to keep your data across devices.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.lead: Study Bro is a free Pomodoro timer. This page explains what data it handles, where it lives and how you can control it.

scope.title: Who this covers
scope.intro: This policy applies to the Study Bro website and app at studywithbro.com, including the guide and legal pages. If you have a question about it, use the Feedback panel in the app.

collect.title: What we store on our servers
collect.intro: Study Bro keeps only what it needs to run the app:

list.1: **Account details:** if you sign in with Google, your name, email address and profile image; if you sign in with an email code, your email address.
list.2: **Tasks:** titles, descriptions, priority, status, tags, due dates and Pomodoro estimates.
list.3: **Focus sessions:** mode (focus, short break or long break), duration, time, and the linked task if any.
list.4: **Sign-in sessions:** a session record for each signed-in browser, which includes its IP address and user agent, and short-lived counters used to limit abuse.
list.5: **Guest data:** when you use the app without signing in, a guest session is created so your tasks and sessions can be saved. It has no email address. If you later sign in, that data moves to your account.
list.6: **Feedback:** the message and type you send, an optional rating, and the name and email only if you enter them. If you are signed in, the feedback is linked to your account.

collect.outro: We do not ask for payment details and the app has no ads.

device.title: What stays on your device
device.intro: Some things are stored in your browser and are not sent to us as content:

list.1: Preferences such as timer settings, clock style, scene, sound choices and volume, kept in your browser's local storage.
list.2: A cookie that remembers your language.
list.3: A cookie that keeps you signed in, whether as a guest or with an account.

partners.title: Services that process data for us
partners.intro: Study Bro relies on these providers. Each handles only what its role needs:

list.1: **Vercel:** hosts the website and API, and provides privacy-friendly page-view analytics.
list.2: **Neon:** hosts the PostgreSQL database where account, task, session and feedback data are stored.
list.3: **Resend:** delivers the one-time sign-in code to your email address.
list.4: **Google:** if you choose Google sign-in, Google shares your name, email and profile image with us. Google Analytics is used only on deployments where it is configured.
list.5: **YouTube:** if you play a YouTube link, the video is embedded from YouTube, which may set its own cookies under its own policy.

partners.outro: We do not sell your data or share it for advertising.

list.1: run the timer, tasks, history and streaks, and sync them across your devices when you are signed in;
list.2: send sign-in codes and keep your session secure;
list.3: read feedback and improve the app, and understand overall usage through analytics.

choices.title: Your choices
choices.intro: You stay in control of your data:

list.1: **Export:** in Settings, under Account, download your account, tasks, sessions and tags as a JSON file.
list.2: **Delete:** in the same place you can delete your account. This permanently removes your tasks, focus sessions, tags and sign-in records. Feedback you sent is kept but is no longer linked to you. Guests can delete their guest data the same way.
list.3: **Clear local data:** clearing your browser's site data removes the preferences stored on your device.

choices.outro: Email sign-in codes expire after 10 minutes.

children.title: Children
children.intro: Study Bro is not aimed at children under 13, and we do not knowingly collect their data. If you believe a child has signed up, tell us through the Feedback panel and we will delete the account.

changes.title: Changes to this policy
changes.intro: If the way Study Bro handles data changes, this page is updated and the date at the top changes with it.

terms.title: Terms of Service
terms.lead: These terms cover your use of Study Bro, a free Pomodoro timer with tasks, focus history and ambient sounds. By using the app you agree to them.

service.title: The service
service.intro: Study Bro is provided free of charge. You can use it as a guest or with an account. Features may be added, changed or removed over time.

use.title: Using Study Bro
use.intro: Please use the app in good faith. In particular:

list.1: Keep your sign-in method secure; you are responsible for activity on your account.
list.2: Do not attack, overload or probe the service, or work around its limits, such as rate limits.
list.3: Do not use the feedback form to send unlawful, abusive or malicious content.
list.4: Do not access other people's data or accounts.

content.title: Your content
content.intro: The tasks, notes and tags you create are yours. We store and process them only to provide the app to you, as described in the Privacy Policy. You can export or delete them at any time.

thirdParty.title: Third-party content
thirdParty.intro: If you play a YouTube link, that content and its playback are governed by YouTube's own terms. Study Bro does not own or control third-party content.

availability.title: Availability and backups
availability.intro: We aim to keep the app running but do not guarantee uninterrupted service. Export your data from time to time if it matters to you.

liability.title: Disclaimer and liability
liability.intro: The Pomodoro timer is a productivity aid, not professional advice.

list.1: Study Bro is provided "as is", without warranties of any kind, to the extent the law allows.
list.2: To the extent the law allows, we are not liable for indirect or consequential losses, or for loss of data or study or work time arising from use of the app.

snake.title: Snake
snake.description: Eat, grow, and don't hit yourself.
snake.instructions: Steer with the arrow keys or WASD, or swipe on a touch screen. Eat the red dot to grow and score 10 points. The snake speeds up as it grows, and hitting a wall or your own body ends the run.
snake.tip: Hug the walls early and keep open space in front of the head.
snake.hint: Arrows / WASD or swipe · Esc to pause

game2048.description: Slide and merge tiles up to 2048.
game2048.instructions: Slide every tile with the arrow keys, WASD or a swipe. Two equal tiles that touch merge into one and add to your score. Reach 2048 to win, then keep going for a higher score. The run ends when the board is full and nothing can merge.
game2048.tip: Keep your biggest tile in a corner and build a descending row along one edge.
game2048.hint: Arrows / WASD or swipe · Esc to pause
game2048.reachedHint: Keep going for a higher score, or finish here.

minesweeper.title: Minesweeper
minesweeper.description: Clear the board without touching a mine.
minesweeper.instructions: Tap a square to open it. A number tells you how many of the 8 neighbouring squares hide a mine. Flag the squares you think are mines (right-click, long-press, or turn on flag mode). Open every safe square to win; your first tap is always safe.
minesweeper.tip: Tap a number whose flags already match it to open all its other neighbours at once.
minesweeper.hint: Click to open · right-click or long-press to flag · Esc to pause

stack.title: Stack
stack.description: Drop sliding blocks to build a tower in 3D.
stack.instructions: A block slides back and forth above the tower. Tap, click or press Space to drop it. Any part that overhangs is cut off, so the tower gets thinner with every sloppy drop. Land it almost exactly on the block below for a perfect drop that keeps its full size.
stack.tip: Watch the block's edge, not its middle, and drop just as the edges line up.
stack.hint: Tap, click or Space to drop · Esc to pause

typingSprint.title: Typing Sprint
typingSprint.description: Type as many words as you can in 60 seconds.
typingSprint.instructions: Type the highlighted English word and press Space or Enter to submit it. Correct words score their length; a wrong word scores nothing. You have 60 seconds. Your speed is shown in words per minute (5 characters = 1 word).
typingSprint.tip: Keep your eyes on the next word while your fingers finish the current one.
typingSprint.hint: Space or Enter submits a word · Esc to pause

aimTrainer.title: Aim Trainer
aimTrainer.description: Hit the targets before they shrink away.
aimTrainer.instructions: One target appears at a time. Click or tap it before its ring shrinks to nothing. Faster hits and longer combos score more. A missed click or an expired target resets your combo. The round lasts 30 seconds and targets get quicker as you go.
aimTrainer.tip: Keep your cursor near the middle of the screen so every target is a short move away.
aimTrainer.hint: Click or tap the target · Esc to pause

brickBreaker.title: Brick Breaker
brickBreaker.description: Bounce the ball and clear every brick.
brickBreaker.instructions: Move the paddle with the mouse, arrow keys or by dragging a finger. Tap, click or press Space to launch the ball. Clear all the bricks to reach the next level. Hitting several bricks without touching the paddle builds a combo bonus. You have 3 lives.
brickBreaker.tip: Hit the ball with the paddle's edge to steer it into the corners.
brickBreaker.hint: Mouse, ← → or drag · Space or tap to launch · Esc to pause
brickBreaker.launch: Tap or press Space to launch

spaceShooter.title: Space Shooter
spaceShooter.instructions: Your ship fires on its own, so just move it: drag with a mouse or finger, or use the arrow keys or WASD. Shoot enemies for points and avoid their fire. Power-ups drop now and then: R is rapid fire, 3 is triple shot, S is a one-hit shield. You have 3 lives and the waves get denser every 400 points.
spaceShooter.tip: Stay in the lower half of the screen so you have time to react.
spaceShooter.hint: Drag, arrows or WASD to move · Esc to pause

memoryMatch.title: Memory Match
memoryMatch.description: Find every matching pair in as few moves as you can.
memoryMatch.instructions: Flip two cards per turn to find matching pairs. Matches stay open, mismatches flip back, so remember where things are. Your score drops with every extra move and every second, so aim for a quick, clean run.
memoryMatch.tip: Open cards in a fixed order at first, so each reveal teaches you something.
memoryMatch.hint: Click or tap cards · Esc to pause

ticTacToe.title: Tic Tac Toe
ticTacToe.instructions: Play five rounds against the computer, you as X. Get three in a row on 3 × 3, or four in a row on 4 × 4. A win scores 3 points and a draw 1; Hard and 4 × 4 each double the points. You and the computer take turns going first.
ticTacToe.tip: Take the centre or a corner first; on Hard a draw is already a good result.
ticTacToe.hint: Click or tap a square · Esc to pause
